blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — nitrofurantoin for uncomplicated ESBL-E cystitis
stem: A stable client has uncomplicated cystitis caused by ESBL-producing E. coli that is susceptible to nitrofurantoin. Which statement best explains why nitrofurantoin may be selected?

options.A: Nitrofurantoin is a preferred option for susceptible uncomplicated ESBL-E urinary infection, while broader agents can be reserved when suitable lower-UTI options are available.
options.B: Nitrofurantoin is preferred because it reliably treats ESBL-E bloodstream infection and renal-parenchymal infection using the same oral regimen used for uncomplicated cystitis.
options.C: Nitrofurantoin should be selected for ESBL-E cystitis without considering susceptibility because resistance to this drug does not occur among urinary Enterobacterales.
options.D: Nitrofurantoin is primarily a respiratory antibacterial, so its use for uncomplicated bacterial cystitis represents an off-label alternative rather than a preferred urinary option.

rationale: Current IDSA 2026 AMR guidance lists nitrofurantoin among the preferred options for uncomplicated urinary tract infection caused by ESBL-producing Enterobacterales when active. The guidance suggests reserving carbapenems and other broader agents for situations in which preferred or suitable alternatives cannot be used and for more complicated or invasive infections. Nitrofurantoin should not be extrapolated to bloodstream or renal-parenchymal infection, and treatment selection still depends on infection site and antimicrobial activity. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Use nitrofurantoin appropriately for susceptible uncomplicated lower urinary infection caused by ESBL-E and avoid extrapolating its role to invasive or renal-parenchymal infection.
source_document_title: IDSA 2026 Guidance on the Treatment of Antimicrobial Resistant Gram-Negative Infections
source_locator: Section 1 ESBL-E, Question 1.1 and rationale: nitrofurantoin is among preferred options for uncomplicated ESBL-E UTI when active; carbapenems are typically effective but are suggested to be reserved for cUTI and other invasive ESBL-E infections when effective uUTI options exist; treatment suggestions assume in-vitro activity.
source_claim_supported: Nitrofurantoin is a preferred active option for uncomplicated ESBL-E urinary infection and should not be generalized to invasive or renal-parenchymal infection.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: understand medication indications and effectiveness; support safe antimicrobial selection.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four options as complete antimicrobial-selection statements of comparable length.
Removed the key-length cue and updated wording to the current 2026 IDSA formulation.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current IDSA 2026 guidance; all options are tightly length-matched.
